runners_data.name: Royal Rhythm
runners_data.note: Won over C&D-equivalent 2m distance on good ground 18 days ago and is in career-best form at 10; Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill yard sends out a conditional in Benjamin Macey, who claims 3lbs — the horse is the natural pace-setter here and any style-fit discount is overridden by the simple absence of any rival willing to press him.|

runners_data.name: Atreides
runners_data.note: Wearing a tongue-tie after a run of placed efforts without winning, Neil Mulholland's eight-year-old has a workmanlike prominence profile and could sit second throughout; his form has been consistent at OR 94 but he has not won in his last five starts, which limits confidence even if the race shape suits.|

runners_data.name: Jefe Triunfo
runners_data.note: Chris Gordon's seven-year-old has been off 96 days and his last run includes a fall (U), so fitness and jumping confidence are the primary questions; suited by good ground with 13 runs on similar conditions, and his natural hold-up style means he will need the pace to be genuine to get involved.|

runners_data.name: County Champs
runners_data.note: Back quickly after just 14 days, this hold-up mare has strong placed form at 2m4-5f on good ground and the longer trip looks ideal; trained by Chris Gordon alongside Jefe Triunfo, her record shows four placings in her last five completed runs and she could be the most dangerous closer if Royal Rhythm does the donkey work.|

runners_data.name: Clever Relation
runners_data.note: Toby McCain-Mitchell takes the ride on this six-year-old who at heart prefers to race from the rear — the horse is shown in midfield on the map only because the cluster of hold-up types compresses the field, not because that is his natural territory; dropping in OR and carrying just 155lbs, but his Fontwell-distance history is all at 2m and shorter, making this step up to 2m5½f an open question.|

runners_data.name: Kings Order
runners_data.note: The youngest and lowest-rated runner at OR 76, James Turner's five-year-old has form at the trip on good ground but has fallen (U) in recent starts and consistency is a concern; naturally a back-marker placed in midfield by necessity given the field shape, and the STYLE_FIT discount applies — he is the one most likely to struggle to assert at any point in the race.|

races.paceDynamic: Royal Rhythm is the sole confirmed front runner in this six-runner field and, with no rival willing or able to press them aggressively from the off over 2m5½f, is likely to control tempo at a measured, sustainable clip around Fontwell's tight, turning track. Atreides will attempt to race prominently and may track Royal Rhythm, but the bulk of the field — County Champs, Jefe Triunfo, Clever Relation, and Kings Order — are natural hold-up types who will be content to stalk from off the pace. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: Clever Relation and Kings Order are genuine back-markers redistributed to midfield on the map, but in reality all four closers will be competing for space behind Royal Rhythm, creating a bunched, steadily-run affair where the leader controls the fractions. This shape — a lone front runner dictating an uncontested tempo with a single prominent tracker — strongly favours horses that can race handily without burning energy early, or those with a powerful late kick that can be deployed from a close enough position when the tempo is honest but not brutal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Royal Rhythm Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Rhythm bowls along in front uncontested and sets a controlled, galloping tempo that suits a staying test.
scenarios.body: Royal Rhythm, dictating every yard on a track that rewards front runners at Fontwell, conserves enough energy to hold on past the last flight; Atreides, tracking in second throughout, is best placed to grab the runner-up spot if the leader fades.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Rhythm's pace proves just quick enough to stretch the field but the leader ties up in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Atreides, lobbing along in second throughout and travelling well within himself, times his challenge to collar the tiring leader between the last two hurdles; County Champs, having raced handily enough from her hold-up position, can finish with purpose on good ground where she has strong placed form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Power Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set is genuinely searching and the hold-up types get enough cover early to produce a strong late run.
scenarios.body: Jefe Triunfo or County Champs, both suited by good ground and the longer Fontwell trip, could unleash a meaningful finishing effort if Royal Rhythm has emptied the tank by the third-last; County Champs in particular has a strong placed record at 2m4-5f on similar ground and handles the track.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Rhythm blunders or capitulates early, scrambling the race order and handing initiative to a opportunist.
scenarios.body: Clever Relation or Kings Order, both natural back-markers running out of their true role in this map, are unlikely to be ideally positioned if the race unfolds at normal pace — but a collapse in front could see an unexpectedly fresh horse emerge late; both are low-rated, lightly-weighted, and untested at this trip.

watchPoints.text: Royal Rhythm — watch for whether Benjamin Macey (conditional, 3lb claim) allows the horse to bowl along at its natural tempo or overrides it; if Royal Rhythm is taken back or meets a hurdle awkwardly, the entire race shape dissolves.

County Champs — quick turnaround of 14 days and Fern O'Brien in the saddle; if she gets a trouble-free run from her hold-up position and the pace is genuine, she is the primary danger to the front runners and worth following in-running.

Kings Order — has a recent fall on his form card (U) and is the least experienced runner here at five years old; watch for jumping errors that could cause interference given he is likely to be racing in a pack of hold-up horses in the back half of the field.

Jefe Triunfo — 96 days off means fitness is unproven; watch how Chris Gordon's charge travels after the halfway point — if he drops away before the straight the trainer has two runners in this race and County Champs becomes the yard's live hope.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Maiden Hurdle  (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Anzac Day
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who needs things to happen late; Jonjo O'Neill Jr. will have to produce a late run from off a single front-runner at Fontwell, where the track's tight turns can suit or hinder closers — his sim-going record of 4/9 on good (no wins, one place) is modest and 32 days off is unremarkable.

runners_data.name: Coastal Command
runners_data.note: 273 days off the track is the dominant concern here, though Nicky Henderson's T14 figure of 1/2 suggests targeted preparation; maps prominent which suits him stylistically given his two third-place finishes, but sim-going on good turf shows only one placing from three hurdle starts.

runners_data.name: Moab
runners_data.note: Henrietta Knight's consistent performer who has placed in five of his last 15 runs on similar going, but his inability to convert from close-up positions is a recurring theme; 16 days since last run keeps him race-fit, and Brendan Powell will use hold-up tactics that depend on late gaps Fontwell doesn't always provide.

runners_data.name: Downtown Nashville
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old with just two hurdle runs (both on good ground, both placed) making him genuinely unexposed at this trip; Olly Murphy's T14 rate of 2/13 is active and Sean Bowen is a high-class booking, but undefined running style creates uncertainty about where exactly he will be positioned in a small field.

runners_data.name: Novelista
runners_data.note: The pace-setter by default in this five-runner field, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) indicates she may be racing out of her natural comfort zone as a confirmed prominent runner rather than a pure front-runner; Warren Greatrex has been in form (T14: 4/13) and James Bowen is competent, yet her sim-going record of 7/14 on similar turf (no wins, three places) tempers confidence in her ability to dictate and hold on.

races.paceDynamic: Novelista is the sole confirmed pace-setter here, and with no other natural front-runner to challenge, she will control the tempo from the front over this 2m3f trip at Fontwell. Coastal Command is mapped prominent but has shown no real pace-forcing tendency in his form, meaning Novelista can dictate at whatever rhythm suits her jockey James Bowen. The hold-up duo of Anzac Day and Moab will be asked to make ground from further back, while Downtown Nashville's undefined style (lightly raced with only two hurdle runs) adds a small unknown. The race shape strongly favours horses with tactical versatility or the ability to travel just off a single uncontested leader — a prominent-to-midfield profile that can close on a horse who has had it all her own way but carries the caveat that Novelista's STYLE_FIT flag suggests her chance should be tempered; the bigger beneficiaries are those able to track and pounce late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Novelista Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Novelista leads comfortably and James Bowen rations the pace to produce a strong-staying gallop that burns off hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Novelista sets a measured pace into the final circuit, building enough of a lead that the hold-up horses cannot reel her in from 2m3f away on good ground; her recent runner-up at 2m (16f) on good suggests stamina at this trip is unproven but she should stay.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Novelista's pace is just quick enough to drain her stamina late, allowing the hold-up horses to reel her in on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Anzac Day and Moab, covered up in the early stages, find the gallop just testing enough to reach their ideal conditions turning for home; their superior stamina profiles over this trip suit a late surge if Novelista has gone too hard.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Murphy's Horse Causes Upset
scenarios.trigger: If Downtown Nashville, lightly raced and unexposed, produces a big step forward under Sean Bowen to quicken clear.
scenarios.body: With only two hurdle runs and an OR of 120, Downtown Nashville remains highly unexposed and Sean Bowen knows how to present a young improver at the right moment; if he slots into a handy position and runs a career-best, his good-ground form (2nd and 3rd at 16f on GOO) puts him in contention.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: No Pace Collapse, Henderson Horse Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Novelista fades abruptly and Coastal Command, fresh from a 273-day break, has been sharpened to peak fitness by Nicky Henderson.
scenarios.body: Coastal Command's long absence is a significant concern, but Henderson's T14 strike rate of 1/2 over this window is encouraging and his two third-place runs at 2m on soft show ability; if he arrives fit and tracks Novelista before asserting, the prominent position could prove decisive.

watchPoints.text: Novelista's STYLE_FIT flag warrants close monitoring at the start — if she is slow away or fails to assert early, the entire pace scenario unravels and hold-up horses Anzac Day and Moab become far more dangerous.

Coastal Command's 273-day absence is a major unknown; watch his paddock condition and early movement — if he travels well within himself in the early stages, his prominent position gives him a live each-way chance despite the layoff.

Downtown Nashville is only two hurdle runs into his career and is entirely unexposed over 2m3f — Sean Bowen's positioning in the first half-mile will reveal a great deal about the stable's intentions and confidence in the horse's stamina.

With only five runners and a single pace-setter, the tempo is entirely at Novelista's discretion — if James Bowen elects to go very slowly to preserve her stamina, the race could become a sprint finish that disadvantages Anzac Day and Moab who need a true test of endurance.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Edgewell
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner with a dominant pace profile, wearing a hood; 4 wins from 15 runs on similar good ground with a strong record at this trip range, trained by Nick Scholfield who has 3 winners from 16 runners in the last 14 days — the tactical fulcrum of this entire race.

runners_data.name: Gata Ban
runners_data.note: Neil Mulholland's hold-up performer has won twice and placed twice in his last five runs on good ground, and his recent course form over similar distances marks him as the most likely finisher if Edgewell is caught; wears a pricker, 14 days since last run, right at his peak.

runners_data.name: Unspeakable
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor takes the ride on a horse returning from 75 days off wearing a tongue-tie; finished second over 26f on good ground in his most recent comparable run and handles this surface well, but the layoff and a modest trainer 14-day record of 0/5 temper expectations.

runners_data.name: The Kings Soldier
runners_data.note: A natural rear-of-field horse that the race shape pushes into a midfield role it doesn't suit — the 0.93 STYLE_FIT flag is a real concern; Oscar Palmer's 7lb claim helps on weight, but 0 wins from 10 runs on good ground and an apprentice in a tactical race over 3m2f are compounding negatives.

runners_data.name: Frankie Faulkner
runners_data.note: Adam Wedge partners a hold-up type whose best efforts came on softer ground (placed twice on soft), making this good surface a genuine query; the horse's natural style is to race at the back, but redistribution into midfield asks a question of a runner already carrying a going concern and 56 days between runs.

runners_data.name: Of Corse I Can
runners_data.note: Bradley Harris's 3lb claim is the headline on a nine-year-old with a modest record — 1 win from 15 runs on good ground and consistently finishing in the 4th-6th bracket; its true hold-up style is compressed into midfield here given the glut of closers, and that mismatch, combined with the lowest OR in the field, makes a winning performance very difficult to construct.

races.paceDynamic: Edgewell is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no rival capable or willing to challenge him for the lead, he will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset over 3m2f at Fontwell. The five remaining runners are all hold-up types by nature, meaning the race will develop as a procession behind Edgewell with the main action concentrated in the final mile as closers try to close down a horse who has had things his own way throughout. Three of those hold-up horses — The Kings Soldier, Frankie Faulkner, and Of Corse I Can — are genuine rear-of-field types who will be forced into a midfield role they don't naturally occupy, as there are simply too many hold-up horses for the race shape to accommodate them all at the back. This setup heavily favours Edgewell to control and potentially steal the race on the bridle, while Gata Ban and Unspeakable — the classiest of the closers — are best placed among the hold-up brigade to launch the most meaningful late challenges; true front-running dominance is the standout profile this shape creates.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Edgewell Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Edgewell dictates an uncontested lead and the hold-up pack fails to close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: Edgewell bowls along at a fair but manageable clip with nothing to worry him early, conserving energy through Fontwell's tight turns before quickening away from the final fence; his strong record on good ground (4 wins from 8 placed runs in similar conditions) makes him a formidable front-running threat.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Him In
scenarios.trigger: If Edgewell's solo lead takes its toll late and the better-rated hold-up horses pounce from the final fence.
scenarios.body: Gata Ban, who has won twice over similar distances on good ground and finished second twice more, is best positioned to chase down a tiring leader if the front-runner has overcooled in the early stages; Unspeakable, dropping in weight at OR 78, also has the profile to pick up strongly in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed hold-up types — forced into midfield — happen to find a better position than expected and travel prominently enough to strike.
scenarios.body: Frankie Faulkner or The Kings Soldier could benefit if the pace is genuinely steady enough to allow them to lobber along in a handy midfield berth and produce a challenge; however, both carry STYLE_FIT discounts given they are racing out of their natural role and trainer form for both is modest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank Outsider Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or tactical chaos disrupts the leaders and a lower-rated hold-up horse collects at long odds.
scenarios.body: Of Corse I Can has shown minor form on good ground and could theoretically collect if multiple runners exit the race or tire dramatically; this is a low-probability collapse scenario rather than a structured tactical shape.

watchPoints.text: Watch Edgewell's jumping — if he makes an early error and loses his uncontested lead, the entire race shape unravels and Gata Ban immediately becomes the dominant force.
Gata Ban is 14 days fresh and Neil Mulholland's trainer strike rate over that 14-day window is 0/8 — a horse in peak condition on paper but a trainer without recent winners to point to.

Unspeakable's 75-day absence is the longest layoff in the field; Christian Williams is 0/5 in the last 14 days, and Jack Tudor will need the horse to strip fit first time out if it is to land a blow at the business end.

The three redistributed hold-up horses (The Kings Soldier, Frankie Faulkner, Of Corse I Can) will be jostling for similar ground in the early stages — watch for crowding or interference as they settle into an unfamiliar midfield role on Fontwell's tight track.

Weight is tightly compressed in this handicap (145–168lbs), meaning the OR differential between Edgewell (92) and Of Corse I Can (69) is real but the conditions favour horses who can dictate rather than those who carry lighter weights into a hold-up position.

runners_data.name: Start Again
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner for Fergal O'Brien, returning after a 106-day break, has strong form at this trip and similar going (8 runs on good, one win five places), but that layoff and a recent pull-up add a fitness and reliability question; Kielan Woods takes over in the saddle.

runners_data.name: Ask A Sainte
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen partners this Olly Murphy-trained six-year-old, who has solid placed form at two miles plus on good ground and won over a similar trip; the trainer is 2/13 over 14 days, suggesting reasonable current yard form, though a pull-up last time out needs explaining.

runners_data.name: No More Bolero
runners_data.note: James Owen's seven-year-old arrives in outstanding form — three wins from the last four outings — with a strong record on good ground (four wins from 11 comparable runs) and Harry Cobden booked; the step up to 2m3f from shorter trips is the only query.

runners_data.name: So Proud
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr. partners this five-year-old, who is by nature a prominent racer but is effectively squeezed out of that position here by the weight of prominent types; racing at OR 103 off a 101-day break, its best form has come when allowed to stride forward, making the midfield position a genuine disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Motazzen
runners_data.note: Henrietta Knight's eight-year-old is the only genuine hold-up horse in the race, running just nine days after its last start and wearing tongue-strap; its good-ground record is poor (0 wins, 2 places from 15 comparable runs) and it needs a very different race shape to the one most likely to unfold.

races.paceDynamic: Start Again is the sole confirmed front-runner and should lead from the outset, setting a measured, uncontested gallop over this 2m3f trip with no rival likely to seriously challenge for the lead. Ask A Sainte and No More Bolero are both prominent types and will sit close behind, creating a compact, well-strung-out early order rather than a contested breakneck pace. So Proud is a genuine prominent racer who is redistributed to midfield here because there is simply insufficient room at the head of affairs for another prominent type — the field holds more front-running and prominent candidates than the race shape can accommodate, with Start Again and No More Bolero the most likely to secure their natural positions. With pace sustainable and the tempo unlikely to be extreme, horses that can travel prominently and produce a sustained galloping finish will be favoured — this race shape suits prominent-to-lead types who stay well, not closers waiting on a collapse that probably will not come.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Start Again leads at a fair pace and the race is run at a steady-to-honest tempo, setting up a staying contest from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Start Again dictates throughout and may prove hard to pass if fresh enough after 106 days off, while No More Bolero's excellent recent form (three wins in last four) makes him the chief danger travelling prominently under Harry Cobden.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Overcomes Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally too slow early and the prominent horses press Start Again, creating a more pressured gallop.
scenarios.body: No More Bolero, in career-best form and stepping up slightly in trip, has the class and fitness edge to wear down Start Again in the straight; Ask A Sainte under Sean Bowen is also well-placed to benefit if the front pair come back to the field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or injudicious jumping disrupts the leaders, opening the door for a late run.
scenarios.body: Motazzen is the only true hold-up horse in the field but has modest recent form, struggling for consistency and running just nine days ago under headgear; the scenario requires an unusually fast pace set by Start Again that burns off the field, which seems unlikely given the lone-leader dynamic.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If So Proud, racing out of its natural prominent role, settles better than expected and produces an unexpected turn of foot.
scenarios.body: So Proud is a genuine prominent type pushed into midfield by the race shape and is unlikely to produce its best racing from further back than it wants; this scenario depends heavily on horses out of role and an atypical race shape, making it the least probable outcome.

watchPoints.text: No More Bolero's trainer T14 record of 2/36 is light but his horse arrives in the form of his life — watch whether Harry Cobden moves him into a challenging position early to exploit Start Again's fitness question after 106 days off.

Start Again's 106-day absence combined with a pull-up on his most recent completed run means fitness and jumping reliability are genuine concerns — watch his jumping in the early stages for any signs of rustiness.

So Proud is racing out of its natural front-of-the-field position; if Jonjo O'Neill Jr. attempts to push forward to reclaim a prominent spot, it could create unexpected early pressure and disrupt the anticipated controlled pace.

Motazzen runs just nine days after its last outing and has a poor record on good ground — watch the market for any unexpected support, which could indicate stable confidence, though the pace shape works firmly against it.

runners_data.name: Jiair Madrik
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins on good ground are the standout form angle here; Donald McCain's yard is quiet (0/15 in 14 days) but this horse is clearly in a purple patch, wears headgear, and as the likely pace-setter at Fontwell his ability to control tempo off a 61-day break is the race's central question.

runners_data.name: Imperial Bede
runners_data.note: Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill have had a quiet recent spell (0/12 in 14 days) but Imperial Bede was back quickly after his last run (14 days) and has a habit of placing without winning (0W2P in similar going); Richie McLernon is well-placed to settle him prominently and wait for the front pair to weaken.

runners_data.name: Midnight Jewel
runners_data.note: A decade-old chaser with 13 runs in similar going, two wins but only one recent success, and connections have been selective (1/3 in 14 days); as a confirmed front-runner, James Bowen will need to decide quickly whether to fight Jiair Madrik for the lead or drop back, and a back-seat role would be out of character for this horse given his profile (headgear worn).

runners_data.name: Martin's Denuo
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with upside and a recent win in his form (F-1114), but his only comparable-going run produced a fourth from just five attempts, and his natural style sits closer to midfield than genuine hold-up; Rian Corcoran (5lb claimer) rides, and in a field this small at a turning track, finding clean daylight from off the pace presents a real tactical challenge.

races.paceDynamic: Jiair Madrik and Midnight Jewel are both confirmed front-runners in a field of just four, guaranteeing a contested early pace as both attempt to establish their favoured lead position at Fontwell over 2m3½f. Jiair Madrik arrives in excellent form (three straight wins) and carries headgear, suggesting connections intend to press forward aggressively, while Midnight Jewel has headgear of their own and a recent win, meaning neither is likely to concede the lead cheaply. The result will be an honest, genuine gallop from the outset — not a dawdle — which stretches the field and tests jumping ability and jumping stamina rather than finishing speed. This race shape strongly favours hold-up or prominent horses capable of travelling within themselves before picking off a fatigued leader, meaning Imperial Bede — the most consistently prominent type — and Martin's Denuo, who can sit off the pace, are the profiles most likely to benefit if the front two burn each other out. The field holds more front-running types than can all dominate, and of the two, Jiair Madrik — on a superior winning streak and sharper form — is most likely to actually secure the front, with Midnight Jewel forced to either sit a close second or capitulate early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Jiair Madrik repels Midnight Jewel's early challenge and settles into a controlled lead inside the first mile.
scenarios.body: Jiair Madrik's three consecutive wins on good ground and in-form handler Donald McCain give him the credentials to sustain a pace he sets himself; at Fontwell's tight, turning circuit a dominant lead can be difficult to reel in from behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Pair Collapse Late
scenarios.trigger: If the two leaders push hard against each other throughout, leaving both vulnerable from the third-last fence.
scenarios.body: A genuine mid-race battle between Jiair Madrik and Midnight Jewel inflates the pace to the point that both tire before the finish, handing an advantage to a horse that has tracked them economically.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Imperial Bede travels smoothly in second or third and finds enough on the run-in to collar the leader.
scenarios.body: Imperial Bede has placed twice at this sort of trip on good ground and Richie McLernon knows how to ration a chaser's effort; a clean jumping round and patient tactics could see him land a decisive blow approaching the last.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Hold-Up Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Martin's Denuo is allowed to sit well off the pace and produce a sustained finishing effort from the final bend.
scenarios.body: Martin's Denuo is a young, lightly-raced type whose form figures include a recent win, but his limited similar-going evidence and true midfield/hold-up profile make him a long shot in a small field where gaps may never materialise at Fontwell's tight layout.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Midnight Jewel immediately challenges Jiair Madrik for the lead at the start — if she does, the pace will be fierce and both front-runners become vulnerable late.
Jiair Madrik is 61 days off the track; if he blows up after his exertions setting the pace, Imperial Bede is best placed to capitalise given his patient tactical ride.

Martin's Denuo is ridden by a 5lb claimer (Rian Corcoran) in only his second chase run at this distance — jumping errors or positional misjudgement in a small, fast-run field could end his chance early.

Midnight Jewel's 13 runs in similar going (2W4P) suggest she handles conditions but her last two starts were fifths; if she is losing her edge, she may crack first when Jiair Madrik presses on from the front.

With only four runners, gaps and traffic are not concerns — the race will likely be run in a strung-out line, meaning Fontwell's tight bends and jumping accuracy become the dominant sieving mechanism rather than finishing speed.

races.name: Free Race Replays On Attheraces.com Mares' Open National Hunt Flat Race
